title: Normal Forecast
summary: Predict what pnorm(), qnorm() and seeded random draws print.
hints: `pnorm()` gives the area *below* a value; the mean of a normal curve has half the area on each side.
`qnorm()` runs the other way: proportion in, score out. Without `mean` and `sd` it uses the standard normal (mean 0, SD 1).
The same seed gives the same draws.

quiz.prompt: The standard normal curve has mean 0. What is the area below 0?
quiz.explain: A normal curve is symmetric about its mean, so exactly half its area lies below it. (0.3989 is the curve's *height* at 0, which `dnorm(0)` gives; height isn't probability.)

quiz.prompt: Three proportions in, three scores out:
quiz.explain: 2.5% of the standard normal lies below −1.96 and 97.5% below +1.96, so ±1.96 cuts off the middle 95%. That's where the 1.96 in a 95% interval comes from. (±1.645 cuts off the middle 90%.) R pads 0 to 0.000000 so the three numbers line up.

quiz.prompt: How much of a normal curve lies within one SD of the mean?
quiz.explain: Area below +1 minus area below −1 leaves the area between them: about 68%. Within two SDs it's about 95% (0.9545); 0.3413 is just the half from 0 to 1.

quiz.prompt: A score of 130 on a scale with mean 100 and SD 15, compared with z = 2 on the standard normal:
quiz.explain: 130 is (130 − 100) / 15 = 2 SDs above the mean, and areas depend only on the z-score. Converting to z and using the standard normal gives exactly the same proportion.

quiz.prompt: Two random draws from the same seed:
quiz.code:
set.seed(1)
a <- rnorm(3)
set.seed(1)
b <- rnorm(3)
identical(a, b)
choices: Error: random numbers can't be compared
quiz.explain: Resetting the seed restarts the generator from the same point, so `b` repeats `a` exactly. That's what makes a simulation reproducible.

quiz.code:
set.seed(1)
a <- rnorm(3)
b <- rnorm(3)
identical(a, b)
quiz.explain: The seed sets the *starting* point. After `a` the generator has moved on, so `b` gets the next three numbers. One `set.seed()` at the top of a script is enough; you don't set it before every draw.
